items.title: A watch that talks back
sentences: When Daniel bought his first smartwatch, he assumed it would simply tell him the time and count his steps.
Within a week, however, the device had started to send him reminders to stand up, breathe and drink water.
At first he found these messages helpful, and he even felt a little proud when he reached his daily targets.
Gradually, though, the constant alerts began to feel like pressure rather than support.
Eventually he turned most of the notifications off, keeping only the one that wakes him in the morning.
Looking back, he admits that the watch taught him more about his own habits than any of its numbers did.

explanation.en: 'The device' replaces 'smartwatch', 'these messages' are the reminders, and 'the constant alerts' and 'the notifications' keep naming them. 'At first', 'Gradually' and 'Eventually' give the time sequence.
explanation.es: 'The device' sustituye a 'smartwatch', 'these messages' son los recordatorios y 'the constant alerts' y 'the notifications' siguen nombrándolos. 'At first', 'Gradually' y 'Eventually' marcan la secuencia.

note.en: Another word for the messages; 'though' contrasts with 'At first'.
note.es: Otra palabra para los mensajes; 'though' contrasta con 'At first'.

note.en: Back to the watch from the start.

items.title: Machines in medicine
sentences: The promise of artificial intelligence in medicine rests on a simple premise: that patterns invisible to a human eye may be obvious to a machine trained on millions of scans.
In certain narrow tasks, such as spotting early signs of disease in an image, that premise has been borne out.
Yet success of this kind tends to obscure a more troubling question, namely what happens when the system is wrong.
A human specialist who misses a diagnosis can usually explain the reasoning behind the error; an algorithm, by contrast, often cannot.
This opacity makes it difficult for doctors to know when to trust a recommendation and when to override it.
Until that difficulty is resolved, many hospitals are likely to treat such tools as assistants rather than as decision-makers.

explanation.en: 'That premise' repeats the opening idea, 'success of this kind' refers to the borne-out premise, 'by contrast' sets the algorithm against the specialist, 'This opacity' names the algorithm's silence and 'that difficulty' names the doctors' problem.
explanation.es: 'That premise' retoma la idea inicial, 'success of this kind' remite a la premisa confirmada, 'by contrast' opone el algoritmo al especialista, 'This opacity' nombra su falta de explicación y 'that difficulty' el problema de los médicos.

note.en: The idea that machines can see hidden patterns.
note.es: La idea de que las máquinas ven patrones ocultos.

note.en: The algorithm is compared with the human specialist.
note.es: Se compara el algoritmo con el especialista humano.

note.en: The algorithm's inability to explain itself.
note.es: Que el algoritmo no pueda explicarse.

note.en: Doctors not knowing when to trust the tool.
note.es: Los médicos no saben cuándo fiarse de la herramienta.
